title: Descriptive Statistics in Excel
unit: Core Unit 1 · Apply Statistical Concepts and Analysis

lesson.html:
By the end of Day 2 you should be able to:

  1. Compute and interpret the mean, median, and mode, and choose the right one for the data.
  2. Compute and interpret range, variance, standard deviation, and coefficient of variation.
  3. Find quartiles, the IQR, and the five-number summary, and detect outliers with the 1.5 × IQR rule.
  4. Build a frequency distribution and a histogram, and describe its shape (symmetric or skewed).
  5. Use Excel functions and the Analysis ToolPak, and cross-check results (quality standard).
  6. Write plain-language insights for a business owner.

Materials you need today

Item File / Location
Branch sales dataset (90 days × 4 branches) Day02/assets/Day02_Branch_Sales.xlsx
Activity template Day02/assets/Day02_Descriptive_Stats_Template.xlsx
Demo video (with captions) Day02/demo/Day02_Demo_Descriptive_Statistics_in_Excel.mp4
Activity sheets Day02_Student_Activities.pdf

Descriptive statistics summarize a dataset with a few numbers and charts, so we can understand it quickly. They answer four questions:

Question Measures
Where is the center? Mean, median, mode
How spread out is the data? Range, variance, standard deviation, IQR, coefficient of variation
What is the position of a value? Minimum, quartiles, percentiles, maximum
What is the shape? Frequency distribution, histogram, skewness

Worked example used throughout this handout: Caloocan branch daily sales (₱) for 7 days:

9,800 11,200 10,500 12,000 10,500 3,200 13,100

Sorted: 3,200 9,800 10,500 10,500 11,200 12,000 13,100 (n = 7)

Mean (arithmetic average)

Mean = sum of values ÷ number of values x̄ = Σx ÷ n

Example: 70,300 ÷ 7 = ₱10,042.86 Excel: =AVERAGE(range)

Median (middle value of the sorted data)

  • If n is odd, the median is the middle value. If n is even, it is the average of the two middle values.
  • Position of the median = (n + 1) ÷ 2 = (7 + 1) ÷ 2 = 4th value → ₱10,500 Excel: =MEDIAN(range)

Mode (most frequent value)

  • ₱10,500 appears twice → mode = ₱10,500 Excel: =MODE.SNGL(range). Use =MODE.MULT(range) when there are several modes.
  • The mode works best for discrete or categorical data, such as the number of transactions or the most popular payment method. Continuous peso amounts rarely repeat, so Excel may return #N/A, meaning no value repeats.

Which average should I use?

Situation Best measure Why
Symmetric data, no extreme values Mean Uses every value
Skewed data or outliers (e.g., the 3,200 flood day) Median Not pulled by extreme values
Categories / most common item Mode The only valid "average" for nominal data

See the effect of an outlier: without the ₱3,200 flood day, the mean jumps from ₱10,042.86 to ₱11,183.33, while the median moves only from ₱10,500 to ₱10,850. The median is resistant to outliers; the mean is not.

Two branches can have the same average and very different consistency. Spread measures how far values are from the center.

Range

Range = Maximum − Minimum = 13,100 − 3,200 = ₱9,900 Excel: =MAX(r)-MIN(r) Easy to compute, but it depends on only two values, so one outlier changes it a lot.

Variance and standard deviation

  1. Find each value's deviation from the mean (x − x̄).
  2. Square each deviation, so negatives don't cancel out the positives.
  3. Add them up. For a sample, divide by n − 1; for a whole population, divide by N.
  4. The standard deviation is the square root of the variance. It is back in pesos, so it is easy to interpret.
x x − x̄ (x − x̄)²
3,200 −6,842.86 46,824,693.88
9,800 −242.86 58,979.59
10,500 457.14 208,979.59
10,500 457.14 208,979.59
11,200 1,157.14 1,338,979.59
12,000 1,957.14 3,830,408.16
13,100 3,057.14 9,346,122.45
Σ 0 61,817,142.86

Sample variance s² = 61,817,142.86 ÷ (7 − 1) = 10,302,857.14 Sample standard deviation s = √10,302,857.14 = ₱3,209.81

Excel Use for
=VAR.S(r) / =STDEV.S(r) Sample data (most business data, e.g., 90 days out of all possible days)
=VAR.P(r) / =STDEV.P(r) The entire population is in the data

Interpretation: "Caloocan's daily sales are typically about ₱3,210 above or below the average of ₱10,043."

Coefficient of variation (CV)

CV = (standard deviation ÷ mean) × 100% = 3,209.81 ÷ 10,042.86 × 100 = 31.96% Use CV to compare consistency between branches of different sizes. A lower CV means more stable sales.

lesson.h: Part 4 — Quartiles, IQR, Five-Number Summary, and Outliers
lesson.html:
Quartiles divide sorted data into four equal parts.

Measure Meaning Excel Example
Minimum Smallest value =MIN(r) 3,200
Q1 25% of values are below it =QUARTILE.INC(r,1) 10,150
Median (Q2) 50% below =MEDIAN(r) 10,500
Q3 75% below =QUARTILE.INC(r,3) 11,600
Maximum Largest value =MAX(r) 13,100

These five values are the five-number summary, which is also what a box plot shows.

Interquartile range (IQR) = Q3 − Q1 = 11,600 − 10,150 = 1,450. It is the spread of the middle 50%, and outliers do not affect it.

The 1.5 × IQR outlier rule

  • Lower fence = Q1 − 1.5 × IQR = 10,150 − 2,175 = 7,975
  • Upper fence = Q3 + 1.5 × IQR = 11,600 + 2,175 = 13,775
  • Any value below 7,975 or above 13,775 is an outlier → ₱3,200 is an outlier.

Excel flag formula: =IF(OR(B2<$F$1,B2>$F$2),"OUTLIER","")

An outlier is not automatically an error. Investigate it first: - Data error (typo, duplicate) → correct it. - Real event (flood, fiesta, payday, promo) → keep it, explain it, and consider using the median.

Never delete data just because it is inconvenient. This is part of applying quality standards and ethical work practices.

lesson.h: Part 5 — Frequency Distribution, Histogram, and Shape
lesson.html:
A frequency distribution groups values into classes (bins) and counts how many fall in each.

Steps

  1. Find the minimum and maximum.
  2. Choose about 5–12 classes of equal width. Example: width ₱4,000 → 0–4,000, 4,001–8,000, …
  3. Count the values in each class: =COUNTIFS(r,">="&lower, r,"<="&upper) or =FREQUENCY(data, bins).
  4. Add the relative frequency (%) = f ÷ n × 100 and the cumulative frequency.

A histogram is a bar chart of the frequency distribution, with bars touching because the classes are continuous. Excel 2016 and later: select the data → Insert → Insert Statistic Chart → Histogram. You can also build a column chart from your frequency table and set the gap width to 0–5%.

Shapes of distributions

Shape What it looks like Mean vs median Skewness (=SKEW(r))
Symmetric (bell-shaped) Mirror image around the center Mean ≈ median ≈ 0 (between −0.5 and 0.5)
Right (positively) skewed Long tail to the right; a few very high values Mean > median > 0
Left (negatively) skewed Long tail to the left; a few very low values Mean < median < 0

Sales data is often right-skewed because of promo days, paydays, and fiestas.

lesson.h: Part 6 — Analysis ToolPak: Descriptive Statistics in One Click
lesson.html:
Enable it once: File → Options → Add-ins → at the bottom, Manage: Excel Add-ins → Go… → ✓ Analysis ToolPak → OK. The Data Analysis button appears at the far right of the Data tab.

Run it: Data → Data Analysis → Descriptive Statistics → OK.

  • Input Range: the data, including headers (e.g., Daily_Sales!$C$1:$F$91)
  • Grouped By: Columns · ✓ Labels in first row
  • Output Range: an empty cell, or New Worksheet Ply
  • ✓ Summary statistics → OK

Output includes Mean, Standard Error, Median, Mode, Standard Deviation (sample), Sample Variance, Kurtosis, Skewness, Range, Minimum, Maximum, Sum, and Count.

⚠️ The ToolPak output is static values. It does not update when the data changes; re-run it after edits. Excel functions update automatically.

Quality check: cross-verify

A professional analyst computes key numbers two ways and confirms they match. Today you compute with functions (Activity 2.1), then with the ToolPak (Activity 2.2), and compare them. If they don't match, look for a wrong range, a missing row, or STDEV.P used instead of STDEV.S. (Integrated: Apply quality standards.)

Numbers alone don't help Aling Nena. Translate them into plain sentences.

Weak Strong
"QC mean = 19,697." "Quezon City sells about ₱19,700 a day, the highest of the four branches."
"Caloocan CV = 21.6%." "Caloocan's sales are the least predictable (CV 21.6%), so stock should have a bigger safety buffer."
"Pasig has 3 outliers." "Pasig had 3 unusual days. The biggest was the 7 March barangay fiesta (₱30,606), so plan extra stock for the next fiesta."

Insight formula: What (the number) + So what (what it means) + Now what (a recommendation).

Term Definition
Mean Sum of values divided by their count
Median Middle value of sorted data
Mode Most frequent value
Range Maximum minus minimum
Variance Average squared deviation from the mean (n − 1 for samples)
Standard deviation Square root of the variance; typical distance from the mean
Coefficient of variation SD as a percentage of the mean; compares relative spread
Quartile A value that divides sorted data into quarters
IQR Q3 − Q1, the spread of the middle 50%
Outlier A value unusually far from the rest (outside the 1.5 × IQR fences)
Frequency distribution A table of counts per class
Histogram A bar chart of a frequency distribution
Skewness A measure of a distribution's asymmetry

• Report a center and a spread together, e.g., "₱19,700 ± ₱3,540 a day".
  • With outliers or skew, prefer the median and IQR.
  • Investigate outliers; never delete them blindly.
  • Cross-check results (functions vs ToolPak), and turn numbers into insights a business owner can use.

Next session (Day 3): Probability, the normal distribution, z-scores, correlation, and simple regression.

activities.html:
On the Stats sheet, enter a formula in every yellow cell (rows 4–20) for all four branches.

Data ranges:

Branch Daily_Sales range Daily_Transactions range
Quezon City Daily_Sales!C2:C91 Daily_Transactions!C2:C91
Marikina Daily_Sales!D2:D91 Daily_Transactions!D2:D91
Pasig Daily_Sales!E2:E91 Daily_Transactions!E2:E91
Caloocan Daily_Sales!F2:F91 Daily_Transactions!F2:F91

Steps

  1. In B4 (Count, Quezon City) type =COUNT(Daily_Sales!C2:C91) → it should give 90.
  2. Complete column B (Quezon City), using the Excel Function Summary table in your handout:
    • Mean =AVERAGE(...), Median =MEDIAN(...), Mode =MODE.SNGL(Daily_Transactions!C2:C91)
    • Min, Max, Range =B9-B8, Sample Variance =VAR.S(...), Sample Std Deviation =STDEV.S(...)
    • CV (%) =B12/B5*100, Q1 =QUARTILE.INC(...,1), Q3 =QUARTILE.INC(...,3), IQR =B15-B14
    • Lower Fence =B14-1.5*B16, Upper Fence =B15+1.5*B16
    • No. of Outliers =COUNTIF(range,"<"&B17)+COUNTIF(range,">"&B18), Skewness =SKEW(...)
  3. Fill columns C, D and E: select B4:B20 → Ctrl + C → select C4:E20 → Ctrl + V. The ranges are relative references, so they shift to the next branch automatically (e.g. C2:C91 becomes D2:D91). Click one cell in column E and confirm it points to F2:F91.
  4. Format the peso values with a thousands separator: Home → Comma Style.

Questions

a) Which branch has the highest mean daily sales? ______________ The least consistent sales (highest CV)? ______________

b) For which branch is the mean much larger than the median? What does that tell you about its shape?

c) Why do we use STDEV.S and not STDEV.P here?

activities.html:
On the Frequency sheet (all branches combined, n = 360):

  1. D4, frequency: =COUNTIFS(Daily_Sales!$C$2:$F$91,">="&A4,Daily_Sales!$C$2:$F$91,"<="&B4). Fill it down to D14.
  2. D15 total: =SUM(D4:D14). It must equal 360. If it doesn't, check your formula; this is your quality check.
  3. E4, relative frequency %: =D4/$D$15*100 → fill down.
  4. F4 cumulative: =D4; F5: =F4+D5 → fill down. F14 must equal 360.
  5. Make the histogram: select C3:D14 → Insert → Column Chart (2-D Clustered Column).
    • Right-click a bar → Format Data Series → Gap Width = 5%.
    • Chart title: Histogram of Daily Sales (all branches). Axis titles: Daily sales (PHP) and Number of days.
  6. (Optional) Try the built-in histogram: select Daily_Sales!C2:F91 → Insert → Statistic Chart → Histogram.

parts.prompt: Write 5 insight sentences in Stats!B23:B27 (What → So what → Now what)

activities.rubric: Accuracy of numbers (5) · Clarity for a non-technical owner (5) · Quality of the recommendation (5)
activities.html:
(Integrated: Lead workplace communication; Facilitate entrepreneurial skills for MSMEs.) As a team, write 5 sentences in the yellow area on the Stats sheet (rows 23–27), using What → So what → Now what:

  1. Which branch sells the most and the least per day (use the mean or median)?
  2. Which branch is the most and the least consistent (use the CV)?
  3. What do the outliers tell us (paydays? fiesta? flood?)
  4. What is the shape of the sales distribution, and which "average" should the owner use?
  5. One practical recommendation (stocking, staffing, promos).

The reporter presents in 2 minutes. Rubric: accuracy of numbers (5), clarity for a non-technical owner (5), quality of the recommendation (5).
